introduction: Vermont’s refundable earned income credit is claimed on the state tax return. Current law distinguishes taxpayers with and without qualifying children.
description: Vermont’s refundable earned income credit is claimed on the state tax return. Current law distinguishes taxpayers with and without qualifying children.

sections.who: Resident or part-year resident eligibility follows federal EITC rules, with a state exception for otherwise eligible people lacking qualifying taxpayer identification numbers. Residency affects the calculation.
sections.get: Current statute provides 38% of federal EITC with qualifying children or 100% without qualifying children, adjusted for the residency-income ratio. Check the filing year’s instructions.
sections.docs:
• Federal EITC calculation.
  • Wage and qualifying family records.
  • Vermont return and residency information.
sections.apply:
1. Select the filing year

    Use the matching Vermont forms and instructions.

  2. Complete the credit calculation

    Apply the relevant child and residency rules, including any identification-number exception.

  3. File and retain evidence

    Keep the federal calculation and state return.
sections.after: The current statutory percentage should not be substituted into a prior-year return without checking that year’s instructions.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Current Vermont EITC statute. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is one percentage used for everyone?
Current law distinguishes qualifying-child and no-child cases.
